{"type":"text","timestamp":1794620549424,"sessionID":"ses_e28494c37ffeI1oVdmjPSrCgfs","part":{"id":"prt_1d7b868a4001UEebtKYYg5GwQx","messageID":"msg_1d7b8487b001HKHMMtUozsO7H1","sessionID":"ses_e28494c37ffeI1oVdmjPSrCgfs","type":"text","text":"The mission almost certainly scores 0. I collected all 7 targets and brought the rover back to base, but the battery ran out before the episode ended.\n\n**What happened:**\n- **Targets:** I sampled t3, t1, t5, d2 (discovered at tick 6), t4 and t2, all before their deadlines. d1 (discovered at tick 11) was sampled at tick 23, two ticks after its deadline, so it only earned its late value. That's 11.5 of 14 possible points before the end-of-mission multiplier.\n- **Return to base:** the rover reached (19.93, 20.04) at tick 25, about 0.09 m from base, well within the 0.75 m radius. Measured wheel slip on bedrock was about 2–4%, and every stop landed within 0.25 m of its target.\n- **Battery:** it read 0.521 at tick 47, the last packet I received. At 0.5 per idle tick it would be 0.021 after tick 48 and reach zero at tick 49. The final packets hadn't arrived when the episode closed, but the arithmetic doesn't leave room for another outcome. Hitting zero sets the multiplier to 0.\n\n**My mistake:** I didn't do a full energy budget early on. Idle drain over 50 ticks costs 25, which leaves 75 for driving and sampling. My route used about 55 wheel metres of driving plus 7 samples at 3 each, about 76 in total, so I was short by roughly 1 unit. I only noticed at tick 25. By then the last sample and the drive home were already queued, and queued commands can't be cancelled.\n\nDropping the late d1 sample alone would have freed about 7.5 energy (3 for the sample plus a shorter drive home). That would have kept the rover alive at base and scored about 11 of 14 (≈0.79) instead of 0. In future I should check the full energy budget before adding each target to the route.","time":{"start":1794620549284,"end":1794620549421}}}
